chapterTitle: Annual Board Examination Section A Simulator 7 (FBISE Class 12 Chemistry)
title: Annual Board Examination Section A Simulator 7 (FBISE Class 12 Chemistry)
subject: chemistry-12

questions.question: What is the total number of elements present in Period 4 of the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: Period 4 fills 4s (2), 3d (10), and 4p (6) subshells, containing 18 elements from Potassium (Z=19) to Krypton (Z=36).

questions.question: Which of the following compounds gives a crimson red flame in flame photometry?
questions.explanation: Strontium salts impart an intense crimson-red color to the flame.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is an active ingredient in eye lotions and talcum powders due to its mild antiseptic properties?
questions.explanation: Boric acid (H₃BO₃) is a gentle non-irritating antiseptic used in eye washes and baby dusting powders.

questions.question: What is the oxidation state of sulfur in Caro's acid (peroxomonosulfuric acid, H₂SO₅)?
questions.explanation: H₂SO₅ has a peroxide bridge (-O-O- where O is -1 each) and three normal oxide oxygens (-2 each); sulfur is at its maximum +6 oxidation state.

questions.question: Which halogen displacement reaction will occur spontaneously?
questions.explanation: Chlorine is more electronegative with higher reduction potential than bromine, easily displacing bromide from aqueous KBr.

questions.question: Which of the following d-orbitals point directly along the Cartesian axes (x, y, z) and experience greater repulsion from axial ligands in an octahedral crystal field?
questions.explanation: The lobes of d_x²-y² and d_z² lie directly along the x, y, and z axes, clashing directly with incoming octahedral ligands and elevating to the higher energy e_g set.

questions.question: The conversion of an alkane to a branched isomer at 300°C in the presence of AlCl₃/HCl catalyst is known as:
questions.explanation: Straight-chain alkanes convert into branched isomers (e.g., n-butane to isobutane) via catalytic isomerization to boost octane numbers.

questions.question: Thermal cracking (pyrolysis) of higher alkanes involves the breaking of:

options.A: C-C and C-H bonds via a free-radical mechanism at elevated temperatures to yield smaller alkanes and alkenes

questions.explanation: Heating long-chain hydrocarbons to 500-700°C cleaves covalent C-C bonds homolytically, generating gasoline-range branched alkanes and alkenes.

questions.question: The conversion of diazonium salts into chlorobenzene or bromobenzene using cuprous chloride (Cu₂Cl₂) or cuprous bromide (Cu₂Br₂) in the corresponding halogen acid is called:
What is the product when methyl chloride reacts with sodium ethoxide (CH₃CH₂ONa)?

options.A: Ethyl methyl ether (CH₃-O-CH₂CH₃) via Williamson synthesis

questions.explanation: CH₃Cl + Na⁺ O⁻CH₂CH₃ → CH₃-O-CH₂CH₃ (ethyl methyl ether) + NaCl (S_N2 Williamson ether synthesis).

questions.question: What is the order of boiling points among isomeric primary, secondary, and tertiary butyl alcohols?
questions.explanation: Branching decreases molecular surface area and weakens van der Waals forces, while also sterically hindering hydrogen bonding; hence 1° > 2° > 3°.

questions.question: Reaction of an aldehyde with semicarbazide (NH₂-NH-CO-NH₂) produces a crystalline:
Kolbe's electrolysis of an aqueous solution of sodium succinate yields which gaseous hydrocarbon at the anode?
questions.explanation: At the anode, succinate undergoes decarboxylation: -OOC-CH₂-CH₂-COO- - 2e⁻ → •CH₂-CH₂• + 2 CO₂ → H₂C=CH₂ (ethene) + 2 CO₂.

questions.question: Nylon-6,6 is a synthetic polyamide manufactured by the condensation polymerization of which two monomers?
questions.explanation: H₂N-(CH₂)₆-NH₂ + HOOC-(CH₂)₄-COOH eliminate water to form poly(hexamethylene adipamide), designated Nylon-6,6 because both monomers contain 6 carbon atoms.

questions.question: Urea is the most widely manufactured and applied nitrogenous fertilizer in Pakistan because of its high nitrogen content of approximately:
questions.explanation: Urea [CO(NH₂)₂] has molecular weight 60 g/mol with 28 g of nitrogen: (28/60) × 100 ≈ 46.6% nitrogen.

questions.question: Photochemical smog (Los Angeles smog) is an oxidizing smog formed on sunny days by photochemical reactions between:

options.A: Nitrogen oxides (NO_x), unburned volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and sunlight, producing ozone and peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN)
options.B: SO₂ and coal smoke in cold damp air

questions.explanation: Automobile exhaust releases NO and hydrocarbons; solar UV splits NO₂ into NO + O, which creates secondary oxidants: ground-level O₃, aldehydes, and eye-irritating PAN.

questions.question: In Fischer Esterification, a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst (conc. H₂SO₄ or dry HCl). Isotopic tracer studies with ¹⁸O prove that:

options.A: The water molecule is formed from the -OH of the acid and the -H of the alcohol
options.B: The water molecule is formed from the -H of the acid and the -OH of the alcohol
options.D: The alcohol oxygen is converted to CO₂

questions.explanation: Labeling alcohol with ¹⁸O (R'-¹⁸OH) reveals that ¹⁸O ends up in the ester (R-CO-¹⁸OR'), proving that acyl-oxygen cleavage occurs and water derives from the carboxylic -OH.
